title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Cavtat, Croatia 2027: Prices & Hotels
metaDescription: Cavtat has two all-inclusive hotels, Remisens Albatros and Epidaurus. See what is included, 2027 price ranges per person, and who should self-cater instead.
content:
## Does Cavtat Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes. Cavtat has two hotels that sell all-inclusive board: **Remisens Hotel Albatros** and **Remisens Hotel Epidaurus**. Both are listed as all-inclusive properties on major booking platforms, and both are run by the Remisens hotel brand. Cavtat has no large, multi-pool resort of the Turkish or Spanish type. These are mid-sized 4-star beach hotels. Other Cavtat hotels, such as Hotel Croatia and Hotel Cavtat, are sold with breakfast, not all-inclusive.

### Remisens Hotel Albatros
The Albatros stands across from the beach at Od Žala, about 800 m from the town centre. It has a large pool with a terrace, tennis courts, a gym, massage services, a mini club and a games room. Water sports such as windsurfing and banana-boat rides are offered on site. Check-in is from 15:00 and check-out at 11:00. It is rated around 3.5 of 5 on Tripadvisor and is the stronger pick for families with children. Guests often mention a mini disco and a swimming school, and some also mention noise.

### Remisens Hotel Epidaurus
The Epidaurus is also rated about 3.5 of 5. It has family rooms with bunk beds and sea-view balconies. Guests describe a wide food choice and activities on the beach for both children and adults. Pick it if you want a waterfront setting over extra facilities.

## What Is Typically Included

All-inclusive in Cavtat follows the standard Croatian pattern. Exact terms differ by hotel and season, so check the hotel's current board description before booking.

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner as buffet meals
- Snacks between meals at the beach, lobby or pool bars
- Local house drinks (wine, beer, soft drinks, coffee) at set hours
- Pool access and children's club activities

Premium spirits, bottled drinks, à la carte restaurants, sunbeds in some cases and water sports usually cost extra. Guests report that food is plentiful but repetitive by the end of a week.

## Price Per Person Per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

These are rough planning ranges for 2027 for two adults sharing a standard room. Prices swing widely by date. A double room at the Albatros has started around €140 per night for some dates, which works out to roughly €70 per person at the low end.

| Option | Peak (July–August) | Shoulder (May–June, September) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive hotel in Cavtat | €85–120 | €55–80 |
| Half-board hotel (Cavtat/Mlini) | €70–100 | €45–65 |
| Private apartment (room only) | €25–45 | €15–25 |
| Apartment plus food and drinks | €60–95 | €40–65 |

The last row adds about €35–50 per day for eating out, with a konoba dinner, café lunch and groceries. For a couple, all-inclusive costs about €20–30 more per person in peak season than half-board. That gap is roughly what lunch and drinks cost anyway, so the upgrade is fair value for heavy drinkers and big eaters. It is poor value for people who skip lunch.

Children are usually discounted heavily. A family of four with kids under 12 often pays the full adult rate for two people plus partial rates for the children, which is where all-inclusive beats eating out. Restaurant prices in Cavtat are among the highest on the Dubrovnik coast.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Alternatives

Other options within reach:

- **Sunny Dubrovnik by Valamar (Babin Kuk, Dubrovnik).** The nearest large all-inclusive hotel, sold on an all-inclusive basis and aimed at families, with a beach location. It is about 20 km from Cavtat.
- **Mlini (about 8 km north of Cavtat).** Hotel Mlini and Hotel Astarea are mainly sold on half-board or bed and breakfast. Do not expect all-inclusive.

As a rule, Cavtat's own two hotels cover the all-inclusive need. The Babin Kuk area is the fallback when both are full in August.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Cavtat

**Good fit:**
- Families with children under 8. Meals are always ready, drinks are covered, and the pool and mini club keep children busy.
- Short stays of 3–5 nights. Nobody wants to spend a long weekend hunting for a table or shopping for groceries.
- Guests arriving by air. Dubrovnik airport is about 15 minutes by road, so transfers are short.
- Groups wanting a fixed budget.

**Better off self-catering:**
- Couples without children. The town's konobas, the harbour promenade and the Račić Mausoleum walk are the reason to come here.
- Stays of 7+ nights, when a buffet gets repetitive.
- Light eaters and people who skip breakfast or lunch.
- Anyone wanting to try Konavle wine and local seafood.

**Opinion:** The all-inclusive board is oversold in Cavtat. The town's main appeal is the old harbour with its restaurants, and a guest at the Albatros eating every meal at the buffet misses most of it. A better plan for most couples is half-board with one or two evenings out, or an apartment.

## Local Tips

- Book the Albatros or Epidaurus early for July and August. With only two all-inclusive options in town, rooms go first.
- Walk or take a taxi into Cavtat's centre. The Albatros is 800 m away, roughly 10 minutes on foot.
- Hotel Cavtat charges for sunbeds, about €8 per person per half day, so factor that in if you are comparing hotels. Ask what the all-inclusive hotels charge for loungers and water sports.
- Dubrovnik is easy to reach by a cheap ferry, a bus from Cavtat's old town, or a taxi. That makes an all-inclusive base here workable for day trips.
- Shoulder season (May, June, late September) has warm sea and the lowest all-inclusive rates, but not every facility is open. Check that the mini club and water sports operate for your dates.

faq.question: Are there all-inclusive hotels in Cavtat?
faq.answer: Yes. Remisens Hotel Albatros and Remisens Hotel Epidaurus both sell all-inclusive board. Other Cavtat hotels, including Hotel Croatia and Hotel Cavtat, are generally sold with breakfast or half-board.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Cavtat per person per night?
faq.answer: Roughly €85–120 in peak season (July–August) and €55–80 in shoulder season, based on two adults sharing a room. Child rates are lower, and exact prices vary by date and room type.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Cavtat?
faq.answer: No, it costs about €20–30 more per person per night in peak season. It pays off only if you eat lunch at the hotel and drink several times a day, or travel with children.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive or an apartment better for a family in Cavtat?
faq.answer: For young children and stays of 3–7 nights, all-inclusive is easier and often cheaper than eating out. For longer stays or with older children, an apartment with groceries is cheaper and offers more variety.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive resort outside Cavtat?
faq.answer: Sunny Dubrovnik by Valamar in Babin Kuk, about 20 km away, sells all-inclusive. Mlini, 8 km from Cavtat, has hotels but mostly half-board.

Expect roughly €85–120 per person per night in peak season and €55–80 in shoulder season. It suits families with small children and short stays. Longer stays for couples are cheaper in an apartment.
